newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai precious metals upbeat on Indian festivals.
newsitem.headline: Dubai precious metals upbeat on Indian festivals.

text.p: Physical gold and silver demand in the Gulf emirate of Dubai is firming on Indian festival and wedding demand and lower prices, Dubai traders said on Sunday.
India's Diwali festival, expected on November 10, and the country's wedding season from mid-November to end February sparks strong jewellery and bullion import demand.
"There is good demand in India for gold and silver, particularly to Delhi, because of the festival season," one trader at a Dubai jeweller said.
Dubai is the main bullion supplier to the Indian gold market, itself the world's largest consumer market.
A good monsoon season this year is also expected to contribute to healthy Indian buying over the coming festival and wedding season as farmers cash in their crops.
Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola bar (TT) -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted by local traders on Sunday at 5,225 ($1,423.70), down from 5,285 dirhams on October 27.
TT bars in the Bombay markets were assessed around $1,650, with the arbitrage opportunity further helped by a steady Indian rupee rate againt the U.S. dollar of 35.45-35.85.
Ten gram gold pieces in Dubai were quoted at 447 dirhams, down six.
Silver was quoted by local traders at 571 dirhams ($155.58) a kg, 17 dirhams down on the week .
"The dollar price is supporting good physical demand in silver and gold," one trader said.
International spot bullion was last quoted on Saturday at $378.00-$378.50 an ounce, its lowest level since early October. ($1=3.67 UAE dirhams)
